wait_time: usually within a day, sometimes several

request.label: Download an archive of your data

steps.title: Open Settings, then Your account
steps.detail: On the web rather than in the app. Settings and privacy, Your account, Download an archive of your data.

steps.title: Confirm your password
steps.detail: You will be asked to re-enter it, and then to confirm a code sent by email or text.

steps.title: Request the archive
steps.detail: There is one button and no options. You cannot choose a date range or a subset.

steps.title: Wait for the notification
steps.detail: It arrives in the app and by email. Most people see it within a day; a large account can take several.

steps.title: Download it promptly
steps.detail: The link expires after roughly a week and the request has to be made again from scratch.

steps.title: Open Your archive.html to browse it
steps.detail: The archive ships with its own offline viewer. Note the space in the filename - that trips up a lot of scripts.

notes: Bookmarks are not included. Likes are, but only as a tweet id and its text, with no author and no date.
Long posts are stored twice: a truncated copy in the main file and the full text in note-tweet.js. Anything reading only the first one silently loses the body of every long post.
Media in the archive is downsized rather than original. The original URLs are in the data, but they only resolve while the post is still live.

muletto_support.status: reads posts, direct messages, likes and followers through the JavaScript wrapper X puts in front of its JSON. Built from the documented archive format; no real X archive has been opened yet

faq.q: Why are the files in my X archive .js instead of .json?
faq.a: Because the archive ships with an offline viewer that loads them as scripts. Each file is a JavaScript assignment - window.YTD.tweets.part0 = [ ... ] - wrapping otherwise ordinary JSON. A JSON parser fails on every one of them until that first line is stripped.

faq.q: Does the X archive include direct messages?
faq.a: Yes, in direct-messages.js for one-to-one conversations and direct-messages-group.js for group ones. They are in plain text.

faq.q: Why are my old tweets truncated in the archive?
faq.a: Two reasons. Retweets are stored as a 140-character summary beginning RT @, with no way to recover the original. Long posts are stored truncated in tweets.js with the full text in note-tweet.js, joined by id.

faq.q: Are bookmarks in the X data archive?
faq.a: No. Likes are included, bookmarks are not, and there is no way to request them.
